binding.desc: AddDynamic subscribes to anomaly lifecycle. When anomaly spawns/activates/gets captured, audio responds automatically. Zero coupling with gameplay code.
binding.label: Event Binding

config.desc: Audio configuration stored in GameInstance - persists across level loads. Contains Wwise Event references and per-anomaly settings.
config.label: Global Config

post.desc: PostAkEvent triggers the Wwise Event on this specific actor. 3D positioned, respects occlusion/attenuation settings configured in Wwise.
post.label: Event Post

retrieval.desc: GetAnomalyAudioConfig returns a Data Asset with all anomaly sound settings. Designers can tweak without recompiling.
retrieval.label: Config Retrieval

settings.desc: Different anomaly types have unique sounds. GetSettingsForAnomaly looks up the specific audio profile - ghostly whispers vs poltergeist crashes.
settings.label: Per-Anomaly Settings

spatial.desc: InitializeAudioSource sets up the AkComponent for 3D positioning. Each anomaly has its own audio emitter for proper spatialization.
spatial.label: Spatial Source

switch.desc: SetSwitch tells Wwise which sound variation to use. One Event, multiple outcomes based on anomaly type. Memory efficient.
switch.label: Wwise Switch

broadcast.desc: Multicast delegate notifies all listeners. Audio manager, UI, gameplay systems all subscribe. No direct dependencies—each system is separate.
broadcast.label: Event Broadcast

interval.desc: Only refreshes enemy list every N seconds, not every frame. GetAllActorsOfClass is expensive - caching prevents performance hits.
interval.label: Cache Refresh

normalize.desc: Converts raw distance to 0-100% range. Inverted: closer enemy = higher value. Audio systems work with normalized values, not world units.
normalize.label: Normalize Distance

threshold.desc: Only broadcasts when proximity changes significantly. Prevents audio system spam from micro-movements. Typically 1-5% threshold.
threshold.label: Change Threshold

dataasset.desc: Pure data container - no logic, just editor-exposed properties. Designers create instances, assign Wwise events and tweak values. No C++ recompilation needed.
dataasset.label: DataAsset Pattern

hysteresis.desc: Start/Stop thresholds prevent audio flickering. Designers tune these per-enemy without code changes. Meta tags add editor validation.
hysteresis.label: Hysteresis Values

wwise.desc: TObjectPtr to Wwise asset. Audio events, RTPCs, switches - all assigned in editor. Zero hardcoded strings. Change audio by swapping asset references.
wwise.label: Wwise Reference

datatable.desc: DataTable holds audio config - which Wwise switch, how long to display subtitle. Separate from actual text for cleaner localization.
datatable.label: Audio Metadata

stringtable.desc: StringTable for dialogue text - Unreal's native localization system. Same AnomalyID key in both tables. Text team edits StringTable, audio team edits DataTable.
stringtable.label: Localized Text

struct.desc: FTableRowBase enables DataTable integration. Each row = one dialogue entry with Wwise switch + duration. CSV import/export friendly.
struct.label: DataTable Row

breathing.desc: Triggers stressed breathing loop. Plays on top of dread layers when enemy is close.
breathing.label: Stress Breathing

dread.desc: Posts a Wwise Event that starts layered ambient dread sounds - low drones, unsettling textures. These layers intensify based on RTPC value.
dread.label: Dread Layers

hysteresis.desc: Two separate thresholds prevent audio flickering. StartThreshold (e.g. 20%) triggers audio ON, StopThreshold (e.g. 10%) triggers OFF. This gap prevents rapid toggling.
hysteresis.label: Hysteresis Thresholds

intensity.desc: Separate RTPC for breathing rate. Scales with enemy proximity.
intensity.label: Breathing Intensity

proximity.desc: This function is called by EnemyPresenceComponent whenever the distance to the nearest enemy changes. ProximityValue is normalized 0-100%.
proximity.label: Proximity Callback

rtpc.desc: Real-Time Parameter Control - sends ProximityValue to Wwise. Controls volume, filter cutoff, and pitch in real-time. Smooth transitions, no hard cuts.
rtpc.label: RTPC Update

cleanup.desc: Clears timer immediately when movement stops. No lingering footsteps after player halts. Clean state management.
cleanup.label: Timer Cleanup

physmat.desc: Critical flag: bReturnPhysicalMaterial must be true. Without it, PhysMaterial is always null - common Unreal audio gotcha.
physmat.label: Physical Material

timer.desc: Only starts footstep timer when actually moving. Prevents phantom footsteps when standing still. Timer auto-repeats at configured interval.
timer.label: Smart Timer

trace.desc: Shoots ray downward to detect floor surface. Uses Visibility channel. Returns surface type for Wwise Switch selection.
trace.label: Line Trace

channel.desc: Uses ECC_Visibility channel for traces. Could also use custom trace channel for more precise audio-only collision detection.
channel.label: Visibility Channel

creaky.desc: Special surface types for horror atmosphere. CreakyWood and CreakyStairs have additional random creaking sounds - player reveals position to enemies.
creaky.label: Creaky Surfaces

mapping.desc: Unreal's SurfaceType enums map to Wwise Switch names. Level designers assign Physical Materials to floors, code automatically plays correct footsteps.
mapping.label: Surface Mapping

physics.desc: Critical flag! bReturnPhysicalMaterial must be true or PhysMaterial will always be null. Common gotcha in Unreal audio integration.
physics.label: Physics Query

ray.desc: Line trace starts from actor's location (feet level). More reliable than character mesh sockets for surface detection.
ray.label: Ray Origin

surface.desc: Returns an FName that maps directly to a Wwise Switch value. FootstepAudioManager uses this to set the correct footstep sound variation.
surface.label: Surface Detection

trace.desc: Traces straight down by m_TraceDistance units. Configurable in editor - typically 50-100cm to handle stairs and uneven terrain.
trace.label: Trace Direction

blueprint.desc: Sound designers can bind Wwise Events directly in Blueprint without touching C++. Iterate on audio faster - no recompile needed.
blueprint.label: BlueprintAssignable

death.desc: Broadcasted when player dies. Triggers death stinger, stops all ambient audio, and starts game over sequence. Critical for audio state management.
death.label: Death Sequence

delegate.desc: DECLARE_DYNAMIC_MULTICAST allows multiple listeners (audio, UI, gameplay) to subscribe. 'Dynamic' means it works with Blueprints, not just C++.
delegate.label: Dynamic Delegate

photoboard.desc: When viewing collected photos, ambient audio ducks and UI sounds activate. Delegates decouple this from hardcoded audio calls.
photoboard.label: Photoboard UI

shutter.desc: Core gameplay mechanic - taking photos. Triggers shutter click sound and photo flash audio. Enemy anomalies react to this sound!
shutter.label: Camera Shutter

zoom.desc: Camera zoom triggers servo motor sound and subtle ambience change. Immersive feedback for player entering 'investigation mode'.
zoom.label: Zoom Audio

hierarchy.desc: Walks up class hierarchy until settings found. BP_GhostAnomaly → AGhostAnomaly → ABaseAnomaly. First match wins - most specific takes priority.
hierarchy.label: Inheritance Walk

reflection.desc: GetClass() returns actual runtime type. For BP_GhostAnomaly inheriting from ABaseAnomaly, this returns BP_GhostAnomaly class.
reflection.label: Runtime Reflection

tmap.desc: TMap<TSubclassOf<ABaseAnomaly>, FAnomalyAudioSettings> - designers map anomaly classes to audio switches in editor. Add new anomaly = add row in DataAsset.
tmap.label: TMap Lookup

hysteresis.desc: Start threshold higher than stop threshold. Enemy at 25% triggers audio, but must drop to 15% to stop. Prevents rapid on/off flickering.
hysteresis.label: Hysteresis Gap

postevent.desc: UAkGameplayStatics::PostEvent triggers audio on this actor. 3D positioned, respects attenuation curves set in Wwise project.
postevent.label: Wwise PostEvent

rtpc.desc: Real-Time Parameter Control. Sends proximity value to Wwise continuously. Controls volume, filter, pitch - smooth modulation, no steps.
rtpc.label: RTPC Update

stopthresh.desc: Lower threshold for stopping audio. Creates hysteresis band that smooths transitions. No audio stutter when enemy hovers at boundary.
stopthresh.label: Stop Threshold

project_akantilado_full_desc: Sound design for a student animation. Two cats chase a golden orb through a jungle. I built 5-layer spatial ambience—canopy birds, mid-level rustling, ground water, wind, wildlife. All foley came from libraries, then I synced everything frame-by-frame to the animation. Made two final mixes: stereo for cinema screening, then 5.1 surround.
project_amorak_block1_content: The creature needed to sound massive. Layered 4 animal recordings—lion, elephant, tiger, hippo. Pitching them down created weight. The hippo texture adds that high-end rasp.
project_amorak_block2_content: The environment follows the camera. Dripping water is close and unsettling. Distant chains suggest something bigger. Binaural panning puts every sound in a specific spot around your head.
project_amorak_block3_content: The creature always wins in the mix. I used dynamic ducking to push the environment down whenever the monster screams or the character breathes.
project_amorak_full_desc:
90-second horror teaser. I did all the audio post-production.

The creature needed to sound massive. I layered 4 animal recordings—lion, elephant, tiger, hippo. Pitched them down to add weight. Made a binaural mix in Reaper using Dear VR Pro and IEM Suite. Final delivery: stereo binaural, 48kHz/24-bit, -16 LUFS. Took 4 weeks.

Dynamics: CLA-76, LA-2A, LA-3A, C6 multiband.
project_audioq_full_desc: VST3/AU sampler plugin I built in JUCE and C++. Drag in any audio file and mangle it with granular synthesis, hand-coded tremolo DSP, TPT zero-delay filters, and a built-in compressor. Every parameter is DAW-automatable. I wrote the tremolo from scratch—per-sample sine LFO for smooth modulation. Open source on GitHub.
project_gradwork_full_desc: Bachelor thesis. I built a Unity game that talks to AI models through a Python server and tested whether they can generate sounds fast enough for games. Tested ElevenLabs, MMAudio, and AudioGen. None were fast enough—the quickest still took over a second. The workaround: cache sounds during loading screens and serve them in under 55ms when needed.
project_not_today_darling_full_desc: Solo audio designer on a 4-player shared-screen racer. No room for subtle stereo—fighting for every decibel of headroom and byte of RAM. Result: loud, chaotic racing that never clips and runs smooth.
project_nottoday_block1_content: Side-scrolling 1-4 player racing game. It's chaotic, loud, and ridiculous. Audio Designer. I did everything audio: recording, sound design, music choice, and implementation.
project_nottoday_block2_content: I didn't want the engines to sound like looped MP3s. I built a graph in MetaSounds where the kart's pitch and rattle intensity change based on speed. You can hear the difference when you drive from carpet to tiles—the sound reacts instantly.
project_pause_and_deserve_full_desc:
Solo horror prototype built in 8 weeks to learn Unreal Engine 5.

Pause freezes the enemy, but each use makes it permanently faster. Audio reacts to player hesitation -- forest ambience, proximity breathing, ticking clock during freeze. MetaSounds + Sound Cues, 100% Blueprints.
project_ray_animation_full_desc: Disco-funk score for a DAE graduation film. The original composer dropped out 8 days before the screening. I wrote the main track and credits music from scratch—brass, slap bass, DJ scratches, Waves J37 tape effects. Frame-synced every hit to Ray's dance choreography. Got a standing ovation at the premiere.
project_richter_full_desc: Sound design for a student earthquake film. All foley recorded from scratch with a Zoom H6—footsteps on wood, concrete, carpet, door sounds, paper handling. I wrote a short orchestral score to match the scene cuts. No commercial libraries. Processed everything in Reaper. Used Cubase for granular stretching.
project_shadow_frames_collab_desc: Collaboration between RITCS (Story), KASK (Music), and Howest DAE (Game Dev).
project_shadow_frames_full_desc:
Horror game where audio is the core mechanic. Players hear anomalies before they see them.

I built the audio systems: footstep surface detection, enemy proximity system, anomaly audio, Wwise integration. Collaboration with RITCS (writers) and KASK (composers).
project_transientica_audiolab_full_desc:
Real-time beatbox recognition system. Control rhythm games with your voice.

Optimized audio buffers and ML pipeline to stay under 60ms latency. Python handles audio analysis, Unity handles gameplay - communication via UDP/OSC.
project_transientica_block1_content: A system that listens to your microphone and classifies sounds in real-time using a custom neural network trained on thousands of samples.
project_transientica_block2_content: Built in Unity with a Python/scikit-learn pipeline. Uses spectral analysis and predictive buffering to achieve <45ms latency.
project_unreal_engine_rebuilder_full_des:
Build automation tool for Unreal Engine.

Unreal Engine sometimes corrupts intermediate files, causing linker errors. This tool creates a "factory reset" for the build—clears cache, regenerates project files, compiles from scratch. Saves hours of manual cleanup.
project_wwise_unreal_fixer_full_desc:
Rescue tool for Wwise-Unreal integration.

When migrating Wwise projects or pulling from Perforce, Unreal often loses asset paths (SoundBanks, Events)—actors go silent. This tool fixes all references in one click.

ambience_zones.desc: Audio changes as you move through different areas of the pub.
ambience_zones.how: Trigger volumes detect where you are. Enter a zone, fade out previous ambience, fade in the new one. Smooth crossfades, no audio jumps.
ambience_zones.result: Walk from bar to bathroom, audio crossfades in 500ms. No pops, no silence gaps.
ambience_zones.title: Ambience Zone System
ambience_zones.what: 5 distinct zones with unique ambient soundscapes: Main Bar, Back Room, Bathroom, Hallway, Storage. Each has specific audio atmosphere.
ambience_zones.why: Each room sounds different. Bathroom: tiles + reverb. Bar: glasses + crowd murmur. Player knows where they are by sound.

anomalies.desc: Semi-randomized disturbances that escalate as the game progresses.
anomalies.env_desc: The space itself warps and distorts. Radio static erupts from nowhere, lights flicker erratically, and the clock accelerates its ticking.
anomalies.object_desc: Chairs rotate on their own, glasses levitate mid-air, and cutlery clatters without cause. Everyday objects begin to defy the laws of physics.
anomalies.shadow_desc: Human silhouettes materialize in the darkness. Shadows peel away from their source objects and move independently. Motion occurs in places where no light source could cast it.
anomalies.title: Anomaly Types

anomaly_audio.alert: Alert (0.5s): Static burst marks the spawn
anomaly_audio.conclusion: No visuals, no UI markers, just sound. Audio is the detection system.
anomaly_audio.description: Every anomaly triggers three audio layers:
anomaly_audio.hint: Hint (1-2s): Directional sound points you there
anomaly_audio.title: 3-Stage Anomaly Detection

anomaly_system.desc: 10 anomaly types. Each has unique audio. 3-stage detection: alert → hint → presence.
anomaly_system.how: Distance-based RTPC drives audio intensity. Directional audio guides player to anomaly. Each anomaly type has unique sound signature for identification.
anomaly_system.result: Playtesters find anomalies by ear. 80% detection rate with directional hints.
anomaly_system.title: Anomaly Audio System
anomaly_system.what: 3 detection stages: Far (general alert), Medium (directional cue), Close (precise location). 10 anomaly types including Levitating Glass, Shadow Movement, Spinning Chair.
anomaly_system.why: Sound is how you find anomalies. Alert signals spawn, hint gives direction, presence confirms location.

audio_systems.delegates_desc: Audio systems communicate through delegates. C++ handles game logic, Blueprint handles audio. Each part works separately. Change one without breaking the other.
audio_systems.rtpc_desc: The more anomalies you find, the more intense everything gets. Ambient sounds ramp up. Your character's breathing gets heavier. Tension builds.
audio_systems.spatial_desc: Full 3D positional audio for anomalies, enemy, and environmental cues. Spatial accuracy is required for gameplay. You can't find threats without it.
audio_systems.switches_desc: Each room has its own ambient layers that crossfade as you move. Bathroom has spatialized toilet and faucet sounds. Footsteps change based on surface. Wood, tiles, concrete.
audio_systems.title: Audio Implementation

block.anomaly_desc: 10 anomaly types, each with unique audio. 3-stage detection. RTPC drives intensity. Directional audio guides player.
block.dialogue_desc: Player actions → audio responses via Blueprint delegates. Camera shot, zoom—each triggers the right Wwise event.
block.enemy_desc: Enemy gets closer, audio intensifies. Dread layers + stressed breathing. System tracks distance, triggers layers. Closer enemy = more intensity.
block.mixer_desc: Switch Containers + RTPC system. More photos = different ambient layers activate. RTPC (0-5) drives Switch Container selection.

challenge1.problem: Multi-institutional student project had workflow problems. Wwise integration broke after Perforce pulls. Unreal compilation took too long, causing downtime.
challenge1.solution: Built Wwise Unreal Fixer and Unreal Engine Rebuilder. Wwise Fixer restores broken integration after Perforce pulls—one click. Rebuilder automates compilation to cut downtime. These help the student team work faster.
challenge1.title: Workflow Tools

challenges.desc: Problems encountered during development and how I addressed them.
challenges.title: Challenges & Solutions

challenges_list.c1_prob: Sounds would rapidly toggle on/off when player stood near trigger edges
challenges_list.c1_sol: Implemented hysteresis: separate start/stop thresholds (Start at 70%, Stop at 60%)
challenges_list.c2_prob: Calculating distance to all enemies every frame was too heavy
challenges_list.c2_sol: Added a caching system that updates the closest enemy reference periodically, not every frame

code_explanations.delegate_how: DECLARE_DYNAMIC_MULTICAST_DELEGATE creates delegate that can be broadcast from C++ and listened to in Blueprint. UPROPERTY(BlueprintAssignable) allows binding in Blueprint.
code_explanations.delegate_what: Definition of multicast delegates for player actions that trigger audio events.
code_explanations.delegate_why: Multicast delegates = multiple listeners react to one action. Audio Manager, UI, gameplay—no direct coupling. Dynamic delegates work with Blueprint. Audio designer has full control, no C++ changes.
code_explanations.footstep_how: Validates owner and world exist, then performs line trace using ECC_WorldStatic channel. Checks object's Physical Material and maps SurfaceType enum to Wwise Switch name (Tiles, Wood, CreakyWood, Concrete).
code_explanations.footstep_what: Function detects surface type under player using line trace downward from player position.
code_explanations.footstep_why: Physical Material = automatic detection. No manual tagging. Enum-to-Switch mapping is a one-time setup. Connects Unreal's surface system to Wwise—configuration, not hardcoded calls. Audio designer modifies Switch names in Wwise, no code changes.
code_explanations.rtpc_how: Validates world exists. Finds AkAmbientSound actor by tag 'AmbientProgressive' (faster and more reliable than string search). Sets RTPC value (0-5) based on important photos. Wwise crossfades automatically.
code_explanations.rtpc_what: Function updates RTPC value in Wwise based on number of photos placed on board.
code_explanations.rtpc_why: RTPC = smooth transitions. I tweak crossfade curves in Wwise, no code changes needed.

concept.desc:
You're trapped in a black-and-white 1960s Irish pub where reality is breaking down. Anomalies appear every 30 to 50 seconds, and sound is your only tool for finding them. Put on headphones and listen carefully. A glass clinks in the corner. Footsteps echo from an empty hallway. A chair scrapes across the floor by itself. Follow the audio to locate each disturbance, then photograph it. You have exactly 12 shots, so choose wisely.

The pub has constant supernatural activity. Glasses levitate off the bar. Shadows detach from their owners and move independently. Chairs spin on their own. The grainy black-and-white aesthetic makes everything feel like a forgotten photograph from decades ago.

Audio is the core mechanic. Mute the game and you can't find anomalies. You won't know where to look, what's happening, or how to survive. Every creak, whisper, and crash is information.

Once you've captured your evidence, race to the corkboard and arrange the photos in the correct chronological order. This is how you piece together what's happening and why. But work quickly. Something is hunting you through the pub, and time is running out.
concept.detailed: You have a Polaroid camera and 12 shots. Anomalies happen every 30-50 seconds. Glasses levitate, shadows move on their own, chairs spin. Audio cues tell you where to look: a glass clinks, footsteps echo from nowhere, a chair scrapes across the floor. Without sound, you're blind. Once you capture the evidence, arrange the photos on a corkboard in chronological order to piece together what's happening.
concept.short: Black-and-white horror game where you photograph paranormal events in a 1960s Irish pub. Sound is your main tool for finding anomalies.
concept.subtitle: Black-and-white psychological horror
concept.title: The Game

dev_tools.fixer_desc: Custom C++ plugin that restores Wwise integration after Perforce pulls. Runs automatically, no manual fixing needed.
dev_tools.rebuilder_desc: Deletes Intermediate and Saved folders, regenerates project files. Fixes linker errors that happen after bad merges. Takes 2 minutes instead of hunting through folders manually.

enemy_presence.desc: Enemy gets closer, audio gets worse. Two layers stack: ambient dread (low drones, textures) and stressed character breathing. Both scale with proximity via RTPC.
enemy_presence.how: OnProximityChanged() receives proximity value (0-100%), starts/stops dread layers, updates RTPC for intensity, adjusts breathing stress. All validated with null safety checks.
enemy_presence.result: Audio intensity scales smoothly with danger level. Layered ambient sounds and stressed breathing respond to proximity without hard cuts.
enemy_presence.title: Enemy Presence Audio System
enemy_presence.what: System tracks enemy distance and triggers audio layers. Closer enemy = more intense audio. Dread ambience and breathing stress scale with proximity.
enemy_presence.why: No hard cuts when enemy moves. RTPC makes it smooth. Breathing layer adds urgency without cluttering the mix.

footstep.desc: Wood, tiles, concrete—you hear the difference. The system detects what you're walking on and plays the right sound automatically.
footstep.how: Physical Material is detected using Unreal's surface system. That gets mapped to a Switch name. Blueprint Audio Manager gets the delegate and plays the right sound in Wwise.
footstep.result: Every footstep matches the surface. Automatic. No manual work. Add a new material in Wwise, it works.
footstep.title: Footstep System: Surface Detection & Audio Routing
footstep.what: Line trace shoots down from the player. Detects the Physical Material. Maps it to a Wwise Switch—Tiles, Wood, CreakyWood, Concrete.
footstep.why: Clean separation. C++ handles detection, Blueprint handles audio. Add new surfaces without touching C++. Audio designer can change Switch names in Wwise without code changes.

gameplay.capture_desc: Use your Polaroid camera to photograph the anomaly. You have limited film, and every reload leaves you vulnerable.
gameplay.connect_desc: Arrange photos on the pin board in the correct order to reveal the truth and reach the good ending.
gameplay.observe_desc: Anomalies appear every 30-50 seconds. Environmental sounds guide you to their location.
gameplay.title: Core Mechanic: Observe → Capture → Connect

media_captions.photos_on_board: Photo board: collected Polaroid snapshots that reveal the story as you arrange them correctly
media_captions.switch_container: Wwise Switch Container setup: controls which ambient layers play based on how many photos are on the board

player_audio.desc: Take a photo, zoom, open the photoboard—each action triggers the right audio through delegates.
player_audio.how: DECLARE_DYNAMIC_MULTICAST_DELEGATE creates delegates that work with Blueprint. UPROPERTY(BlueprintAssignable) allows binding in Blueprint. Multicast means multiple listeners can react to one action.
player_audio.result: Adding new audio is easy. No hardcoded calls. Audio designer changes sounds in Wwise, player code stays untouched.
player_audio.title: Player Audio System: Delegate-Based Communication
player_audio.what: PlayerCharacter (C++) defines multicast delegates. When you take a photo or zoom, the delegate broadcasts. Blueprint Audio Manager listens and plays the sound.
player_audio.why: PlayerCharacter doesn't know audio exists. Audio Manager doesn't know player logic exists. Test and change each independently.

project_metrics.desc: Production statistics and technical implementation scope.
project_metrics.how: 12+ C++ classes for audio systems, 8+ Blueprint audio managers, 200+ Wwise events/switches/RTPCs, 5 location zones, 10 anomaly types.
project_metrics.result: Stable audio across all sprints. Designers adjust parameters in Data Assets without code changes.
project_metrics.title: Project Scale & Technical Metrics
project_metrics.what: Sprint 3/5 production phase. Multi-institutional collaboration. Extensive C++ and Blueprint implementation with Wwise integration.
project_metrics.why: Audio is core to gameplay, so each system needs to work independently. I can update footsteps without touching enemy audio or anomalies.

achievements.data: Exposed all audio parameters to designers via Unreal Data Assets
achievements.flicker: Implemented hysteresis thresholds for audio states to prevent rapid on/off toggling
achievements.opt: Reduced CPU usage by caching enemy distance calculations and using event-based updates

audio_systems.enemy: Proximity-driven tension system with hysteresis to prevent audio flickering
audio_systems.footsteps: Physics-based surface detection via raycasting with velocity-based intervals
audio_systems.mixing: Real-time RTPC modulation of breath and heartbeat based on threat level
audio_systems.spatial: 3D audio cues guiding players to hidden paranormal events

rtpc.desc: More photos on the board, more tension. Ambient intensity ramps up as you progress.
rtpc.how: When you place a photo, UpdateAmbientRTPC() finds the AkAmbientSound actor (tagged 'AmbientProgressive') and sets the RTPC value. Wwise crossfades between ambient layers based on that value.
rtpc.result: Tension builds smoothly as you progress. Tweak curves in Wwise, atmosphere adapts automatically.
rtpc.title: Dynamic Tension System: RTPC-Driven Ambience
rtpc.what: RTPC value (0-5) controls ambient layers in Wwise. PhotoboardWidget tracks how many photos you've placed. More photos = higher RTPC value = more intense ambience.
rtpc.why: RTPC gives smooth transitions between tension states. No audio jumps. I control crossfade curves in Wwise without touching code.

wwise_arch.desc: Switch Containers work with the RTPC system. More photos collected = different ambient layers activate.
wwise_arch.how: PhotoboardWidget sends RTPC value. Wwise uses that to pick the right Switch state and crossfade between layers.
wwise_arch.result: Ambient responds to player progress. This is partial implementation. Full system will have more layers and complexity.
wwise_arch.title: Wwise Setup: Switch Containers & Photoboard Integration
wwise_arch.what: RTPC value (0-5 from photos) drives Switch Container selection in Wwise. Each Switch state has different ambient layers. RTPC handles smooth crossfades, Switch Containers handle structural changes.
wwise_arch.why: Switch Containers give discrete layer control. RTPC gives smooth transitions. Together: structural changes (different ambient sets) and intensity progression.
